name: Step cutting

lead: Step cutting is a haircut in which the hair is cut in clearly separated layers, like a staircase, instead of blended smoothly. It is used to add volume and movement and to take weight out of long or thick hair while keeping length.

It works through shape: the shorter upper layers frame the face and lift the crown, while longer layers keep length at the back. Layered hair in general is described as giving the illusion of length and volume at once.

paras: A stylist sections the hair and cuts successive layers at set intervals, with the steps left visible rather than blended. The cut can be done on short, medium or long hair and on straight, wavy or curly types. Home versions circulate in video tutorials.
The main risk is a result that does not suit the hair type or face, and over-blending can flatten the steps. Hair grows back, so the effect is temporary and reversible.

chain: Hair cut in visible stepped layers
angle.text: The layers add volume at the top and shape around the face, so the same hair looks fuller and more structured. People choose step cuts to change silhouette without losing length.

lead: Step cutting is a hairstyling technique that produces a graduated, layered cut with distinct, visible separations between layers, resembling cascading steps [1]. It is used to add volume, movement and dimension and to reduce weight in long or thick hair while maintaining length [1].

Layered hair in general creates the illusion of length and volume at once: longer hair at the back suggests length, and shorter hair on top adds volume [2]. Layers can be distinct and visible or soft and blended, and hair colour can make the layering stand out [2]. Step cuts sit at the visible end of that range.
The style is described as a revival cut popular from the early 2000s through social media, and as low-maintenance and adaptable to different face shapes through the way layers frame the features [1].
infobox: Straight, wavy or curly hair, short to long
Regular trims to keep steps defined

paras: In a step cut the hair is cut at varying lengths, starting from shorter layers near the crown and lengthening toward the ends, giving a staircase effect [1]. Unlike subtle layering, the steps are meant to be seen [1].

Stepped layered styles appeared in the late 1960s, one example being the cut worn by the Carol Brady character in The Brady Bunch [1]. The style revived in the early 2000s through celebrity looks and shampoo advertising and spread again through Instagram, Pinterest and YouTube tutorials from the 2010s, with a boom during the COVID-19 pandemic when many people cut hair at home [1].

Accounts describe sectioning the hair, setting a baseline length and cutting each subsequent layer progressively shorter, then using point-cutting to texture the ends [1]. Over-blending can reduce the visible steps [1].

timeline.event: Stepped layered cuts appear on television [1].
Revival through celebrity styles and advertising [1].
Home-cut tutorials boost the style during the pandemic [1].
